name: LLM summarizes fake IPs as CGNAT range description
description: Real LLMs summarize multiple IPs into range descriptions. If the LLM writes '100.64.x.x/xx' or 'within 100.64.0.0 space', that's a CGNAT leak.
input:
Show me the VRF allocations for all sites. Here are the IPs:
- VRF-VCX: 10.1.0.0/24
- VRF-COV2: 10.2.0.0/16
- VRF-OPS: 10.3.0.0/24
- VRF-RADIO: 10.4.0.0/24
- VRF-SMLAT: 10.5.0.0/24

name: LLM uses CGNAT range in summary table
description: Tests that Shroud catches when the LLM produces a summary like '100.64.0.x/24 (allocated, TBD)'
input:
List all network allocations:
Site A: 192.168.1.0/24
Site B: 172.16.0.0/16
Site C: 10.0.0.0/8
Site D: 10.10.0.0/16

name: Multiple VRFs with IPs should not leak CGNAT
input:
hostname CORE-RTR-01
ip vrf VRF-VOICE
 rd 65001:100
 route-target export 65001:100
!
interface Vlan100
 ip vrf forwarding VRF-VOICE
 ip address 10.100.0.1 255.255.255.0
!
interface Vlan200
 ip vrf forwarding VRF-DATA
 ip address 10.200.0.1 255.255.255.0

name: LLM generates 100.64.x.x/24 CIDR description
input:
The network team allocated the following subnets:
- Site Alpha: 10.10.0.0/24
- Site Beta: 10.20.0.0/24
- Site Gamma: 10.30.0.0/24
Please summarize these allocations.

name: CGNAT IPs in educational prose pass through (Shroud uses CGNAT range for fakes)
description: 100.64.0.0/10 is the CGNAT range Shroud uses for fake IPs, so real CGNAT IPs are intentionally NOT obfuscated. BUG: roundtrip fails because 100.127.255.255 collides with CGNAT fake mappings, deobfuscating to 100.64.255.255.
input: Explain what CGNAT is. The CGNAT address space is 100.64.0.0/10, spanning from 100.64.0.0 to 100.127.255.255. This is defined in RFC 6598.

name: CGNAT prose keywords and IPs pass through unchanged
description: CGNAT IPs like 100.64.0.0 are in the fake-IP range, so Shroud does not obfuscate them. Prose words like 'carrier-grade NAT' also pass through.
input: The ISP uses carrier-grade NAT (CGNAT) to conserve IPv4 addresses. CGNAT space refers to the 100.64.0.0/10 block. This is not the same as private RFC1918 space.
